stem: A vehicle costing Rs 5,00,000 is depreciated under the written-down value (WDV) method at 20% per annum. Given that (0.8)^3 = 0.512, what is the book value of the vehicle at the end of 3 years?

per_option_rationale.rationale: WDV book value after n years = Cost x (1 - rate)^n = 500000 x (0.8)^3 = 500000 x 0.512 = 256000.
Uses straight-line: 500000 - 3 x 100000 = 200000 (treating 20% of original cost as annual charge).
Applies WDV for only 2 years: 500000 x (0.8)^2 = 500000 x 0.64 = 320000; or miscalculates (0.8)^3 as 0.48 giving 240000, an arithmetic slip in the power.
Deducts 20% of original cost (100000) for each of 3 years but subtracts only 2 years worth: 500000 - 2*100000 = 300000, a period-count error combined with wrong base usage.

explanation: WDV method: each year depreciation is applied to the remaining book value, giving a geometric decay. Book value after n years = Cost x (1 - r)^n = 500000 x (0.8)^3 = 500000 x 0.512 = Rs 2,56,000.

explanation_sections.punchline: WDV depreciation follows geometric decay: book value = Cost x (1 - rate)^n.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify method: WDV (reducing balance). Formula: BV = C x (1-r)^n. Map: C=500000, r=0.20, n=3. Use given: (0.8)^3=0.512. BV=500000*0.512=256000.
explanation_sections.lesson: WDV applies the rate to the declining balance, so use the exponential formula, not the linear subtraction used for SLM.
explanation_sections.timing: 50 seconds. Trap: using SLM (linear) instead of WDV (exponential) formula.
